q.q: Which Constitutional Amendment Act is known as the 'Mini-Constitution' of India?
q.x: The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 is referred to as the 'Mini-Constitution' due to the massive number of changes it brought to the constitutional text. It added the words 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity' to the Preamble. It also introduced Fundamental Duties for citizens.

q.q: Who is the ex-officio Chairman of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) in India?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
q.x: Under Article 64 of the Constitution, the Vice-President of India serves as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. They do not hold any other office of profit during this tenure.

q.q: Which article of the Constitution empowers the President to seek an advisory opinion from the Supreme Court?
q.x: Article 143 confers upon the President the power to consult the Supreme Court on any question of law or fact that is of such nature and such public importance that it is expedient to obtain the opinion of the Court. The Supreme Court may choose to report its opinion, but such advice is not binding on the President.

q.q: Which Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains provisions related to the disqualification of members of Parliament and State Legislatures on grounds of defection?
q.x: The Tenth Schedule, popularly known as the Anti-Defection Law, was added by the 52nd Amendment Act of 1985. It sets the process by which legislators may be disqualified on grounds of defection by the Presiding Officer of the house.

q.q: The 'Writs' jurisdiction of the Supreme Court of India is derived from which Article?
q.x: Article 32, known as the 'Heart and Soul' of the Constitution by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, empowers the Supreme Court to issue writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights. High Courts derive similar power under Article 226.

q.q: Who acts as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
q.x: The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. They preside over the proceedings of the upper house. They do not hold any other office of profit.

q.q: Which article of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to impose President's Rule in a state?
q.x: Article 356 allows for the imposition of President's Rule in a state if the constitutional machinery fails. It is also known as State Emergency.

q.q: Who acts as the Chairman of the National Integration Council (NIC) in India?
q.x: The Prime Minister of India serves as the Chairperson of the National Integration Council. The council was established to address problems of communalism, casteism, and regionalism in the country.

q.q: Which schedule of the Indian Constitution was added by the 1st Amendment Act, 1951, to protect land reform laws from judicial scrutiny?
q.x: The Ninth Schedule was introduced to provide a 'safe harbor' for laws related to land reforms and abolition of zamindari, shielding them from judicial review. However, the Supreme Court later ruled in the I.R. Coelho case that laws placed in the Ninth Schedule after 1973 are open to judicial review if they violate basic structure principles.

q.q: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the 'Uniform Civil Code' for the citizens?
q.x: Article 44 is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy and directs the State to endeavor to secure for the citizens a Uniform Civil Code throughout the territory of India.

q.q: The fundamental duties in the Indian Constitution were incorporated on the recommendation of which committee?
q.x: Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act in 1976. This was done based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee. They are listed under Article 51A.

q.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to promulgate ordinances during the recess of Parliament?
q.x: Article 123 of the Indian Constitution grants the President the power to issue ordinances when Parliament is not in session. These ordinances have the same force and effect as an Act of Parliament but must be approved within six weeks of the reassembly of Parliament.

q.q: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the establishment of a 'Joint Session' of both Houses of Parliament?
q.x: Article 108 allows the President to summon a joint sitting of both houses of Parliament to resolve deadlocks on ordinary legislation. The joint sitting is presided over by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

q.q: Which language was the first to be granted the status of a 'Classical Language' in India?
q.x: Tamil was the first language to be declared a Classical Language by the Government of India in 2004. Other languages have since been added to this list.

q.q: Which amendment to the Constitution lowered the voting age from 21 to 18 years?
q.x: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act of 1988 lowered the voting age for elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies from 21 to 18 years. This came into effect in 1989.

q.q: Who acts as the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
q.x: The Vice-President of India serves as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. They preside over the proceedings of the upper house.

q.q: In which year was the first general election held in independent India?
q.x: The first general election in independent India was held between October 1951 and February 1952. This marked the beginning of India's journey as a democratic republic.

q.q: Who appoints the Chief Justice of India?
q.x: The Chief Justice of India is appointed by the President of India. This appointment is made under the provisions of the Constitution.

q.q: Which part of the Indian Constitution is referred to as the 'Magna Carta' of India?
q.x: Part III of the Indian Constitution, which contains the Fundamental Rights, is described as the Magna Carta of India. It guarantees civil rights to all citizens and protects them against arbitrary state action.

q.q: What is the minimum age required to become a member of the Lok Sabha in India?
q.x: According to Article 84(b) of the Constitution, a person must be at least 25 years of age to qualify for election as a member of the Lok Sabha. For the Rajya Sabha, the minimum age is 30 years.

q.q: Who is the constitutional head of the Indian Union?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
q.x: Under Article 52 of the Indian Constitution, the President is the head of the Indian state. While the Prime Minister is the head of government, the President is the formal constitutional head.

q.q: Who is considered the head of the Indian State and holds the highest office in the country?
q.x: The President of India is the head of the Indian State and the first citizen of the country. They hold the highest office and act as the formal executive head. All executive actions are taken in their name.

q.q: The concept of 'Single Citizenship' in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the constitution of which country?
q.x: India adopted the concept of single citizenship from the British Constitution. Unlike the USA, where individuals hold both national and state citizenship, Indian citizens only hold citizenship of the country as a whole.

q.q: What is the minimum age prescribed for a person to become a member of a Gram Panchayat?
q.x: As per Article 243F, the minimum age required to contest elections for a member of a Gram Panchayat or any local self-government body is 21 years.

q.q: Which fundamental right was abolished by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act?
q.x: The Right to Property was removed from the list of Fundamental Rights by the 44th Amendment in 1978. It was converted into a legal right under Article 300A.

q.q: Which part of the Indian Constitution deals with Fundamental Rights?
q.x: Fundamental Rights are contained in Part III of the Constitution, spanning from Article 12 to Article 35. These rights are guaranteed to all citizens of India.

q.q: A 'Joint Sitting' of the Parliament can be called by the President for which type of bills?
q.x: Under Article 108, the President can summon a joint sitting of both Houses if a bill passed by one House is rejected by the other, or if there is a disagreement on amendments, or if more than six months elapse without passage. This provision applies only to ordinary bills, not to Constitutional Amendment Bills or Money Bills.

q.q: The 'Basic Structure' doctrine, which limits the power of Parliament to amend the Constitution, was formally propounded in which landmark case?
o: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
Minerva Mills v. Union of India
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
q.x: In the 1973 Kesavananda Bharati case, the Supreme Court ruled that while Parliament has the power to amend the Constitution, it cannot alter its 'basic structure'. This established a significant check on the legislative power of the Parliament.

q.q: The concept of 'Procedure Established by Law' in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from which country?
q.x: While the Indian Constitution follows a mix of concepts, the phrase 'Procedure Established by Law' (found in Article 21) was borrowed from the Constitution of Japan. However, through judicial interpretation in the Maneka Gandhi case, the court essentially brought it closer to the 'Due Process of Law' standard found in the US Constitution.

q.q: The 'Basic Structure' doctrine, which limits the Parliament's power to amend the Constitution, was first propounded by the Supreme Court in which case?
o: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
Minerva Mills v. Union of India
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
q.x: The Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) established the Basic Structure doctrine. It held that while Parliament has the power to amend the Constitution, it cannot alter its core or essential features. This remains a cornerstone of Indian constitutional law.

q.q: What is the total number of members in the Rajya Sabha representing states and union territories?
q.x: The maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha is 250, but it currently has 245 members. Of these, 238 represent states and union territories, while 12 are nominated by the President.

q.q: Which constitutional amendment reduced the voting age from 21 to 18 years?
q.x: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act of 1988 lowered the voting age for elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies from 21 years to 18 years. This amendment came into effect in 1989. It was a significant step toward empowering the youth of the country.

q.q: Which amendment is known as the 'Mini Constitution' of India?
q.x: The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 is often called the Mini Constitution because it introduced significant changes to the Constitution. It added the words 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity' to the Preamble.

q.q: In the context of the Indian Parliament, what is the 'Guillotine' process?
o: A motion to remove the Speaker
A process where undiscussed demands for grants are put to vote at the last day of budget discussion
A method to adjourn the house sine die
The power of the President to veto a bill
q.x: Guillotine is a parliamentary procedure used during the budget session. When the time allotted for discussion on the budget concludes, the Speaker puts all outstanding demands for grants to the vote of the House at once, without further discussion. This ensures the budget process is completed within the session timeframe.

q.q: Which among the following is the final interpreter and guardian of the Indian Constitution?
q.x: The Supreme Court of India is the highest judicial authority and the final interpreter of the Constitution. It has the power of judicial review to check the constitutionality of legislative and executive acts.

q.q: Which Fundamental Right cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency as per the 44th Amendment Act?
o: Right to Life and Personal Liberty
q.x: The 44th Amendment Act of 1978 ensured that Articles 20 and 21 (Right to Protection in respect of conviction for offences and Right to Life and Personal Liberty) cannot be suspended during a National Emergency.

q.q: Which constitutional amendment added the words 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity' to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution?
q.x: The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976, often referred to as the 'Mini-Constitution', amended the Preamble to include the terms Socialist, Secular, and Integrity to define the nature of the Indian State.

q.q: Which committee recommended the inclusion of Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution?
q.x: The Swaran Singh Committee was set up in 1976 to make recommendations about fundamental duties. Based on its report, the 42nd Amendment Act was enacted in 1976, adding Part IV-A (Article 51A) to the Constitution. Originally, ten duties were included, and an eleventh was added later.

q.q: Who appoints the Chief Justice and other judges of the Supreme Court of India?
q.x: The President of India appoints the Chief Justice and other judges of the Supreme Court. The appointment is made after consultation with such judges of the Supreme Court and of the High Courts as the President deems necessary.

q.q: The concept of 'Concurrent List' in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the constitution of which country?
q.x: The Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution, which distributes powers between the Union and States, includes a Concurrent List. This concept, along with the provision for a Joint Sitting of the two houses, was borrowed from the Australian Constitution.

q.q: The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are borrowed from the constitution of which country?
q.x: The concept of Directive Principles of State Policy was incorporated into the Indian Constitution from the Irish Constitution. They are listed in Part IV of the Indian Constitution.

q.q: How many members can the President nominate to the Rajya Sabha?
q.x: The President of India can nominate 12 members to the Rajya Sabha from fields such as literature, science, art, and social service. This power is granted under Article 80 of the Constitution.

q.q: Under the provisions of Article 356, what is the maximum duration a President's Rule can remain in force, provided it is periodically approved by Parliament?
q.x: While President's Rule is initially valid for six months, it can be extended for a maximum period of three years with parliamentary approval every six months. Beyond three years, it requires a constitutional amendment, such as the precedent set during the Punjab crisis. It is not an indefinite power.

q.q: How many languages are presently recognized in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution?
q.x: The Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution originally contained 14 languages. Over time, several amendments have increased this number, and it currently lists 22 recognized languages of India.

q.q: What is the minimum age required to become the Governor of a State in India?
q.x: According to Article 157 of the Indian Constitution, a person must be at least 35 years of age to be eligible for appointment as a Governor. This is the same age requirement as the President of India.

q.q: The 'Office of Profit' disqualification for a Member of Parliament is primarily decided by whom?
o: The President in consultation with the Election Commission
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
q.x: Under Article 102(1)(a), a person shall be disqualified if they hold an office of profit under the Government of India or the Government of any State. The decision on such disqualification is made by the President, but the President must act according to the opinion of the Election Commission.

q.q: What is the term of office for a member of the Rajya Sabha?
q.x: Members of the Rajya Sabha are elected for a term of six years. One-third of the members retire every two years, making it a permanent house.

q.q: Who is the ex-officio Chairman of the National Integration Council?
q.x: The National Integration Council (NIC) is a body chaired by the Prime Minister of India. It was constituted to address the problems of communalism, casteism, and regionalism in India. Membership includes Union Ministers, State Chief Ministers, and leaders of political parties.

q.q: The Tenth Schedule of the Indian Constitution, popularly known as the 'Anti-Defection Law', was added by which amendment?
q.x: The 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1985 added the Tenth Schedule to the Constitution. It provides for the disqualification of members of Parliament or State Legislatures on the grounds of defection from their political party.

q.q: Article 262 of the Indian Constitution deals with which of the following matters?
o: Adjudication of disputes relating to waters of inter-state rivers
Coordination between States through Inter-State Council
Special provisions for Delhi and Puducherry
q.x: Article 262 empowers the Parliament to provide by law for the adjudication of any dispute or complaint with respect to the use, distribution, or control of the waters of, or in, any inter-state river or river valley. It also provides that neither the Supreme Court nor any other court shall exercise jurisdiction over such disputes.

q.q: The power of Judicial Review in India is vested in:
o: Both Supreme Court and High Courts
q.x: Both the Supreme Court (under Article 32 and 131-136) and the High Courts (under Article 226) possess the power of judicial review to declare laws or executive actions unconstitutional if they violate the fundamental rights or constitutional provisions.

q.q: The concept of 'Directive Principles of State Policy' in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from which country?
q.x: The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are enumerated in Part IV of the Indian Constitution. This feature was adopted from the Irish Constitution, which had originally copied it from the Spanish Constitution.

q.q: Which landmark Supreme Court judgment established that the 'Basic Structure' of the Constitution cannot be amended by the Parliament under Article 368?
o: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
Minerva Mills v. Union of India
Waman Rao v. Union of India
q.x: The 1973 Kesavananda Bharati case introduced the 'Basic Structure' doctrine, limiting the Parliament's power to amend the Constitution. It held that while Parliament can amend any part, it cannot alter the essential features of the document. This is a foundational pillar of Indian constitutional law.

q.q: Which fundamental right cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency?
o: Right to Life and Personal Liberty
q.x: Under the 44th Amendment Act, the rights guaranteed under Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended even during a proclaimed national emergency. Article 21 ensures the protection of life and personal liberty.

q.q: Under the Indian Constitution, the power to create a new All-India Service lies with:
q.x: Article 312 empowers the Rajya Sabha to create new All-India Services if it passes a resolution supported by a two-thirds majority of members present and voting. This is a special power exclusively vested in the upper house of Parliament.

q.q: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Duty as mentioned in Part IV-A of the Indian Constitution?
o: To protect and improve the natural environment
To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals
q.x: The Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Amendment. Voting in elections is considered a democratic right or obligation, but it is not listed as a Fundamental Duty under Article 51A of the Constitution.

q.q: What is the maximum gap allowed between two sessions of the Parliament in India?
q.x: Article 85 of the Constitution stipulates that there should not be a gap of more than six months between two consecutive sessions of Parliament. Consequently, the Parliament must meet at least twice a year.
